purpose: Define command families as recursive namespaces where intermediate family nodes group commands and may carry metadata/help without being executable commands themselves.

topics.name: Recursive Command Namespaces
topics.purpose: Define command families as recursive namespaces where intermediate family nodes group commands and may carry metadata/help without being executable commands themselves.

semantics.recursive_rule: Command namespaces may contain nested command namespaces and executable leaf/subcommands.
semantics.family_rule: A family root is non-executable unless it separately declares executable command semantics.
semantics.directory_rule: A directory may mirror command namespace structure for implementation/storage, but directory presence does not itself create command semantics.
semantics.extensibility_rule: Recursive families allow new modality branches such as files, images, audio, video or code without flattening the namespace.
semantics.identity_rule: Concrete command identity is the explicit canonical command path, not an arbitrary filesystem path.

invariants.rule: q-family roles, backend aliases, targets, command namespaces and help metadata remain explicit and do not derive authority from model/backend output.

hard_gates.condition: namespace family root executed without declared command semantics
recursive namespaces flattened into unrelated peer commands where hierarchy is canonical
command identity inferred from filesystem path only
namespace separator semantics inconsistent within same command tree

references.purpose: Command paths are semantic namespace addresses.
